title: Validation and Likelihood-Ratio Calibration of the Italian Ritvo Autism Asperger Diagnostic Scale-Revised (RAADS-R).
abstract:
PURPOSE: Italian psychometric evidence on the RAADS-R has been limited. This case-control validation examined the reliability, structure, and measurement invariance of the Italian RAADS-R, its discrimination between autistic and non-autistic adults with candidate cut-offs and likelihood-ratio (LR) bands, subscale contributions, gender differences, and AQ convergence.
METHODS: Sample 1 comprised 376 autistic adults referred to a specialized adult-autism service and diagnosed by blind multidisciplinary assessment, compared with 376 self-declared non-autistic community adults; Sample 2 comprised 354 adults with self-reported previously established diagnoses and 354 comparison adults, matched on age within gender. Analyses covered reliability, CFA/bifactor/ESEM structure, invariance, ROC analysis with cross-sample threshold application, LR bands, a Group × Gender MANCOVA, and AQ convergence.
RESULTS: Internal consistency was excellent (ω = 0.98); a strong general factor (ω = 0.96-0.97) indicated that the DSM-5 subscales describe content rather than distinct dimensions. In Sample 1, AUC was 0.91 and the candidate cut-off of 92 gave sensitivity 0.89 and specificity 0.81; Sample 2 yielded 104 (sensitivity 0.94, specificity 0.77). Across samples, 92 favored sensitivity and 104 specificity. Four LR bands graded the score (≤ 70, 71-91, 92-136, ≥ 137). Autistic women reported higher sensory scores than men, with item-level invariance supported. RAADS-R and AQ totals correlated strongly (r = .86).
CONCLUSION: The Italian RAADS-R is a reliable screening aid within multidisciplinary assessment. Because accuracy was estimated against community adults, the cut-offs and LR bands are preliminary, require validation in consecutive clinical samples, and should not be used to rule out autism when clinical suspicion exists.

journal.name: JOURNAL OF AUTISM AND DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS
